html:
SMTO-WEB-0027 — Your sources disagree about this detail

GUID: f9cdce2f-b9b6-5f39-b840-d0e5f8888afa
Slug: research-fact-conflicted
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • The pages SMTO read give different answers for this detail, so it can't be stated as one settled fact. Both versions are still saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the run to finish. SMTO sends the answer back to the Model and asks it to report that the sources disagree instead of picking one. The check blocks answers that state one value as settled while the sources conflict.
  2. If you know which source is the most reliable, such as the maker's official page, ask SMTO to check that page for this detail. A clear reading from the right source can settle the detail with proof.
  3. If a disagreement is acceptable, tell SMTO it may report conflicting details as unconfirmed. SMTO can then show both readings instead of stopping the answer.

What success looks like

  • The answer either shows the detail with a trusted source or clearly says the sources conflict.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to choose one value and leave out the source that disagrees.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof rejected a non-UNCERTAIN claim that selects a fact recorded as CONTRADICTED (conflicting observations across sources).

What this means

  • A non-uncertain claim selects a fact recorded as CONTRADICTED. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • A non-uncertain claim selects a fact recorded as CONTRADICTED.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the contradictory observations and their exact subject and revision scope.

How to fix it

  • Raised as research_fact_conflicted in _verify_fact. Present the field as UNCERTAIN so it renders as 'conflicting observations', or resolve the conflict with a supported, recorded observation; do not pick one value and hide the conflicting evidence.
  • Preserve the conflicting evidence and qualify the field instead of choosing an unsupported preferred value.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • The answer discloses the conflict or uses a supported resolution backed by retained observations.

What not to do

  • Do not choose the preferred observation and hide the conflicting evidence.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
